messages:
elena_support: FYI inbound from support — Acme Labs hitting a sudden wave of 502/504 + client timeouts on hosted since ~08:22 UTC. They say it started when they kicked off a large export job.

maya_oncall: Pulling traces and infra metrics now. Initial look: request queue depth hit the hard limit and continuous-batcher backlog spiked. p95/p99 tail latency jumped on gateway.

elena_support: Customer notes ~800-900 sustained concurrent requests during the export. They see 'backend read timeout' and 'request canceled' in client logs.

ryan_sre: Metrics snapshot: ingress_queue_depth (per-host) = 1024 (limit = 1024), dequeue_latency_p99 = 4.2s, batcher_pending_tokens ~= 75k, avg_batch_size down (starvation). Router started early rejects around 08:24 UTC.

alex_eng_runtime: @ryan can you paste the gateway/batcher logs? suspecting KV cache spin-up + long-seq batching causing thrash.

ryan_sre: Logs pasted:
```
2026-03-15T08:23:12Z ERROR request_handler.go:412 dequeue failed: queue depth limit reached
2026-03-15T08:23:12Z WARN batcher.go:201 backlog=75643 pending_tokens=3200000
2026-03-15T08:23:12Z ERROR gateway.go:88 backend timeout: 1m0s exceeded
2026-03-15T08:23:13Z DEBUG kvcache_manager.go:145 evicting prefix warmups due to memory pressure
```

maya_oncall: Immediate mitigations applied at 08:30 UTC: bump soft per-tenant queue soft_limit -> 1500 for 10m, enable reject-rate for sequences > 1024 tokens, enable smaller-model fallback for hosted tier for long requests. Deployed via `deploy-bot` canary.

deploy-bot: [deploy] canary rollout: model-fallback v1.3 -> 8 hosts at 08:31 UTC (auto rollback disabled).

elena_support: Customer accepted temp throttle + fallback; errors reduced but intermittent 502s persist on heavy backfill. They asked for a clear runbook and a fix.

alex_eng_runtime: Preliminary root cause: continuous batching scheduler allowed large long-sequence jobs to accumulate, KV cache warmups + eviction thrash increased processing time per batch causing backlog growth until ingress queue hit hard caps. Two things amplified it: (1) tenant colocation on same pool as latency-sensitive workloads, (2) batcher admission doesn't account for pending token count across requests.

ryan_sre: Repro script and steps (can reproduce in staging):
1) ramp 3000 concurrent connections to gateway
2) send requests at 200ms intervals with seq_len=2048 and normal short bursts mixed in
3) observe batcher pending_tokens climb, dequeue stalls, router early reject -> 502/504 after ~40s

elena_support: Next actions:
- write short customer-facing note about recommended patterns for bulk exports (stagger long sequences, use dedicated capacity / private for heavy jobs)
- update support playbook with mitigation steps (soft_limit bump, enable fallback, notify customer)
- schedule eng PR for batcher admission / per-tenant isolation

alex_eng_runtime: I'll own the PR. Plan: implement dynamic admission that uses pending_token budget and per-tenant token quota, plus an opt-in per-tenant isolation flag. Branch: `batcher/admit-tokenbudget-2026`.

maya_oncall: We'll monitor telemetry for 2 hours and follow up. Assigning follow-up ticket to ENG-RUNTIME/RYAN/ELENA. :thumbsup:

elena_support: Closing customer loop now; will reopen if anything recurs. Thanks team.
